title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page as far as it can be read: U is a group object acting on a U-torsor P over T. μ ↪ U is a distinguished subgroup (18). Put U_0 = U/μ (19) and P_0 = P/μ, so P_0 is a U_0-torsor and q: P → P_0 is the quotient map. Π is a fundamental (profinite or discrete) group. 𝓔 is an extension group, apparently of μ by Π, related to π_1(U_0,1) by (20), with E/Π ≅ π_1(U_0,1). There is a compatible square 𝓔 → P, 𝓔_0 = 𝓔/μ → P_0. Grothendieck is preparing to describe groupoids attached to Teichmüller-type towers through 'Π-groupoids with operator group μ'.

(21) He equips the fundamental groupoid Π_1(P_0) with an '𝓔-structure', a homomorphism 𝓔 → Aut(id_{Π_1(P_0)}). In modern terms, for each object x_0 ∈ P_0 the group 𝓔 acts freely on the right of every Hom(x_0,y_0) through its action at x_0. It acts freely on the left through its action at y_0. The two actions are related by ℓ·γ_{x_0} = (^ℓγ)_{y_0}·ℓ, i.e. (^ℓγ)_{y_0} = ℓγℓ^{-1}. This is the familiar mechanism by which the orbit maps of a group action, U_0 → P_0 (u ↦ u·x), send π_1(U_0) into the vertex groups compatibly with transport along paths. It is a 'centre-like' (Gottlieb-type) action, here enlarged to the extension 𝓔 and twisted by conjugation. So the groupoid becomes a groupoid with a 'band' of operators that is compatible up to inner twisting.

Second part. The pull-back of Π_1(P_0) along 𝓔 → P → P_0 is identified with the contracted product Π_1(P) ∧_Π 𝓔, i.e. C' ∧_Π 𝓔. Grothendieck then claims that C_0, the pull-back of Π_1(P_0) along 𝓔_0 → P_0, can be built purely algebraically from C'. The input is C' with its structure of Π-groupoid with operator group μ. The next page carries this out: μ acts on C' ∧_Π 𝓔 by transport of structure and acts freely on its set of objects. The quotient by μ inherits a groupoid structure, and 'plus de doute c'est C_0'. This is an algebraic description of the fundamental groupoid of a quotient torsor, i.e. passing from P to P/μ, in terms of the cover's groupoid plus a free group of operators. It is a groupoid-level version of the exact-sequence/extension bookkeeping for π_1 of a quotient.
errors: No real error. The freeness of the 𝓔-actions on Hom(x_0,y_0) is asserted without justification; it needs injectivity of 𝓔 → π_1(P_0,x_0), which presumably follows from the setup on the previous pages.

With ^ℓγ = ℓγℓ^{-1} read literally, (^ℓγ) is an element of the vertex group at y_0 and not of 𝓔. The notation conflates γ ∈ 𝓔 with its image γ_{x_0}; the intended meaning (transport of the operator along ℓ) is clear.

ideas.what: Group 𝓔 acting on the identity functor of a fundamental groupoid (natural operators on each vertex group, compatible with transport up to conjugation)
ideas.modern_name: Action on the identity functor / Gottlieb-type central action of π_1 of a structure group; banded groupoid structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gottlieb (1965) for the evaluation-subgroup aspect; Giraud (bands, 1971) for the categorical form
ideas.where_published: Related notions (liens, operator groups on groupoids) in SGA1 and Giraud; Teichmüller groupoids are discussed in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Pull-back of a fundamental groupoid along a map of object sets identified with a contracted product C' ∧_Π 𝓔
ideas.modern_name: Base change of groupoids / contracted (balanced) product of groupoids with group actions

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of the quotient torsor P/μ reconstructed algebraically as a quotient of C' ∧_Π 𝓔 by the free μ-action
ideas.modern_name: Quotient of a groupoid by a free group of operators (orbit groupoid); fundamental groupoid of a quotient

deep.surprise_reason: This is technical groundwork: operator structures on fundamental groupoids, contracted products, and quotients by free actions. It is standard groupoid manipulation in service of the Teichmüller groupoid project, with no new result or unexpected connection.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'dire [?] si' is possibly 'Ceci dit' or 'disons'; the handwriting is ambiguous.

Second part: 'par l'application qui ... l'un des sujets' is unclear; it is more likely 'par l'application q, est l'un des objets [?]' or similar, referring to the object sets of the groupoid Π_1(P) ∧_Π 𝓔.
'dis que cette C_0' is likely 'Je dis que cette C_0'.
Bottom line: likely 'C' muni des structures de Π-groupoïde à groupe d'opérateurs μ, [crossed out: et de la structure dict. (13)] ... en effet comme'.
